record.file_problem: Only repository metadata, README, and file list were provided; source files and linked project pages were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the project replicates the original work, describes difference-based refusal-vector extraction and runtime ablation, and reports refusal outcomes on additional models.
record.gate_note: Rows use only outcomes stated in the README. The file list names scripts and result artifacts, but their contents and results cannot be inferred from those names.
record.test_reason: The README reports replicating difference-in-means refusal-vector extraction and residual-stream ablation on seven instruction-tuned models. It gives judge-scored harmful compliance after ablation, which bears directly on V1. It also compares single-vector ablation with small-subspace ablation, which bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author concludes refusal structure is not universal: some models have one dominant removable direction, while others (LLaMA-3.2 1B/3B, partly Phi-3-Mini) spread refusal across a low-rank subspace. The author also notes the work describes empirical structure, not mechanistic causality.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes paired harmful/safe prompts, layer-wise residual-stream differences, and runtime ablation, and says the project replicates the original work. It does not specify enough detail to verify the full original intervention protocol; it also includes weight orthogonalization and comparisons across model families.
record.method_sensitivity: The README states that results depend on prompt construction, but gives no prompt-stratified results.

fits_no_version.finding: Cohen's d separability and cross-layer cosine similarity analyses of refusal vectors are listed, with heatmap figures, but no results are stated in the README.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise geometry and separability of the refusal direction across model families.

record.problems: The README gives group-level ranges rather than per-model outcomes; Phi-3-Mini is explicitly partial. It provides no uncertainty estimates, baseline compliance rates, or benchmark details, and says the harmful/safe prompt data are not included. Its own limitations note that compliance uses an external LLM judge and results depend on prompt construction.
record.rows_left_out: No other outcome rows were stated in the provided README. The file list includes analysis artifacts and scripts, but their contents were not provided and were not treated as results.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; per-model results; any quantified capability retention.
Weight orthogonalization was run, but the README states no refusal or compliance outcome for the edited weights.
Affine and cone formulations; the subspace rank needed; no numeric result for the subspace condition.

missing.what: Per-model compliance, coherence and benchmark values for runtime ablation and for weight orthogonalization, including compliance after the weight edit (bears on V2).
missing.locator: docs/refusal_across_models.md, docs/qwen.md, docs/llama_1b.md (GitHub Pages; not provided)

missing.what: Compliance rate under multi-vector subspace ablation, and the subspace rank used.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available; it is an unreviewed personal project. The original-source rule does not exclude it: it builds on the Alignment Forum precursor post but is an independent replication. The record's 'challenges' label for V1 in the LLaMA-3.2 group is changed to 'limits_scope'. The effect is partial (refusal weakened, not absent), and no baseline is given to show no effect. Compliance is scored by an LLM judge, and the author says results depend on prompt construction.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report adding the direction to induce refusals, nor establish ablation at every layer and position.
Weight orthogonalization and benchmarking are mentioned, but no result states that a weight edit removed refusal.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation adds robustness.
The README compares single-vector ablation with a small subspace, but does not test affine or cone formulations specifically.
No result separates harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
Testing multiple model families is reported, but transfer across languages, base-to-instruct models, or variants is not tested.
No result compares refusal training methods or training stages.
